standard.title: Automotive Vehicles — Tyres for Agricultural Vehicles and Their Trailers — Specification (First Revision)
standard.sector: Transport Engineering / Automotive Tyres, Tubes and Rims

sectional_committee.name: Automotive Tyres, Tubes and Rims Sectional Committee

standard.description: This standard specifies the requirements, dimensions, load ratings, speed categories, markings, and physical performance testing (such as plunger strength, load/speed endurance, and dimensions) for new pneumatic tyres designed for use on agricultural vehicles (such as agricultural tractors, implements, power tillers, and their trailers). It covers diagonal (bias) ply and radial ply tyres.
standard.scope: This standard specifies the requirements, dimensions, load ratings, speed categories, markings, and physical performance testing (such as plunger strength, load/speed endurance, and dimensions) for new pneumatic tyres designed for use on agricultural vehicles (such as agricultural tractors, implements, power tillers, and their trailers). It covers diagonal (bias) ply and radial ply tyres.

certification.description: Strict Statutory Mandatory Certification. Under the 'Pneumatic Tyres (Quality Control) Order' (QCO) issued by the Ministry of Heavy Industries / DPIIT, Government of India, and CMVR Rules 95A and 95B, all pneumatic tyres for agricultural vehicles, tractors, power tillers, and trailers must conform to IS 13154:2015 and carry the mandatory BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark). Manufacturing, importing, or selling non-certified agricultural tyres in India is a punishable statutory offense under the Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 2016. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable to automotive components.
requirements: Every tyre must be clearly molded on its sidewall with the BIS Standard Mark (ISI Mark) along with the manufacturer's registered licence number (CM/L) and classification/load-index codes.

Grounded in dimensional tables, inflated tyres must satisfy specified geometric limits including design section width, minimum section width, maximum overall width, design overall diameter, minimum overall diameter, and maximum overall diameter depending on the tire size code.

Tyres must undergo physical plunger tests where a hemispherical steel plunger (such as 16 mm diameter) is forced into the tread face of an inflated tyre. The tyre must absorb a specified minimum energy before failure or show no penetration/rupture.

Tyres are subjected to dynamic testing on drum-testing machines where the tyre is rotated under a specified percentage of its maximum load rating (e.g. 100% and above) at specified speeds for prescribed durations (endurance test) without developing structural failures such as separation of plies, cord breakage, or tread chunking.
Each tyre must include a molded tread wear indicator to provide a visual cue when the tyre tread depth reaches its critical wear limit, enhancing on-road traction and safety.
